title: If the office hours function is missing from a Spell Action, the code defaults to office hours being on
content:
A.1.10.2.4.12.3.3.4 asks validators to "verify that the office hours function matches the Executive Document," and notes the behaviour when it is absent: "If this function is missing from the Spell Action, the code will **default to the true state (office hours on)**."

Office hours restrict when a Spell may be executed — A.1.10.2.4.8.3.5 gives the voter-facing wording as "can only be executed between 14:00 and 21:00 UTC, Monday - Friday." So the default produced by omission is the *constrained* case, not the permissive one.

This is fail-safe defaulting done correctly, and the direction is the entire point. A forgotten function yields a Spell that can only execute during supervised hours — inconvenient, possibly requiring a delay, but not dangerous. Had the default been the reverse, the same omission would silently produce a Spell executable at 3am on a Sunday with nobody watching, which is precisely when an attacker would want to cast it.

The general principle is that the absence of a decision should not resolve to the more permissive behaviour, because absence is what happens under time pressure, distraction and inexperience. It parallels the Executive Sheet initializing confirmation fields to "Unconfirmed" (A.1.10.2.4.2.3.1): in both cases the empty state means *not yet permitted* rather than *permitted*.

Validators still check the function against the Executive Document rather than relying on the default, since a Spell whose office-hours behaviour contradicts what voters were told is a mismatch regardless of which direction it errs in.
description: A.1.10.2.4.12.3.3.4 documents a fail-safe default where omission produces the more restrictive behaviour, so a forgotten function narrows the execution window rather than widening it.
